Tomato with Bacterial Spot.name: Bacterial spot
Tomato with Bacterial Spot.advice: Remove and destroy infected leaves. Avoid overhead irrigation and do not work in the field when plants are wet. Spray Copper oxychloride 3 g per litre every 7 to 10 days. Use disease-free seedlings and rotate crops.

Tomato with Early Blight.name: Early blight
Tomato with Early Blight.advice: Remove affected lower leaves and spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre every 10 days. Mulch the soil, avoid wetting the leaves, and rotate crops.

Tomato with Late Blight.name: Late blight
Tomato with Late Blight.advice: This spreads fast in cool, wet weather. Spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre at the first signs and repeat after 7 to 10 days. Remove and destroy badly infected plants and do not irrigate in the evening.

Tomato with Leaf Mold.name: Leaf mold
Tomato with Leaf Mold.advice: Improve air flow: widen spacing, stake plants and prune the lower leaves. Reduce humidity and spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre or Copper oxychloride 3 g per litre.

Tomato with Septoria Leaf Spot.name: Septoria leaf spot
Tomato with Septoria Leaf Spot.advice: Remove infected lower leaves. Spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre or Copper oxychloride 3 g per litre every 7 to 10 days. Avoid overhead watering, mulch the soil and rotate crops.

Tomato with Spider Mites or Two-spotted.name: Spider mites
Tomato with Spider Mites or Two-spotted.advice: Wash the underside of leaves with a strong jet of water. Spray neem oil 5 ml per litre or wettable sulphur 3 g per litre. Keep plants well irrigated because mites thrive in hot, dry, dusty conditions.

Tomato with Target Spot.name: Target spot
Tomato with Target Spot.advice: Remove infected leaves, improve air flow between plants and spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre. Avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.name: Yellow leaf curl virus
Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.advice: There is no cure. Pull out and destroy badly affected plants. Control whitefly, which spreads the virus, with yellow sticky traps and neem oil 5 ml per litre. If whitefly is heavy, spray Imidacloprid 0.3 ml per litre. Use virus-resistant varieties next season.

Tomato Mosaic Virus.name: Mosaic virus
Tomato Mosaic Virus.advice: There is no cure. Remove and destroy infected plants, wash hands and tools after touching them, and control aphids with neem oil 5 ml per litre. Use certified disease-free seed.

Healthy Tomato Plant.name: Healthy
Healthy Tomato Plant.advice: The leaf looks healthy. Keep checking your plants every few days, water at the base of the plant and keep the field clean.

Potato with Early Blight.name: Early blight
Potato with Early Blight.advice: Spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre at the first sign of spots. Remove infected leaves, avoid evening irrigation and rotate crops.

Potato with Late Blight.name: Late blight
Potato with Late Blight.advice: This spreads fast in cool, cloudy, humid weather. Spray Metalaxyl + Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre immediately and repeat after 7 to 10 days. Remove and destroy infected plants. Do not store tubers from badly infected plants.

Healthy Potato Plant.name: Healthy
Healthy Potato Plant.advice: The leaf looks healthy. Keep checking for spots, especially in cool and humid weather.

Corn (Maize) with Cercospora and Gray Le.name: Gray leaf spot
Corn (Maize) with Cercospora and Gray Le.advice: Rotate crops and plough in crop residue after harvest. If the attack is severe, spray Propiconazole 1 ml per litre. Use resistant hybrids next season.

Corn (Maize) with Common Rust.name: Common rust
Corn (Maize) with Common Rust.advice: It is usually mild. If it is heavy before tasseling, spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre or Propiconazole 1 ml per litre. Use resistant hybrids next season.

Corn (Maize) with Northern Leaf Blight.name: Northern leaf blight
Corn (Maize) with Northern Leaf Blight.advice: Spray Mancozeb 2.5 g per litre or Propiconazole 1 ml per litre at the first symptoms. Rotate crops and use resistant hybrids.

Healthy Corn (Maize) Plant.name: Healthy
Healthy Corn (Maize) Plant.advice: The leaf looks healthy. Keep checking the crop regularly.

Bell Pepper with Bacterial Spot.name: Bacterial spot
Bell Pepper with Bacterial Spot.advice: Remove infected leaves and spray Copper oxychloride 3 g per litre every 7 to 10 days. Avoid overhead irrigation and use disease-free seedlings.

Healthy Bell Pepper Plant.name: Healthy
Healthy Bell Pepper Plant.advice: The leaf looks healthy. Keep checking the crop regularly.

Healthy Soybean Plant.name: Healthy
Healthy Soybean Plant.advice: The leaf looks healthy. Keep watching for pests such as caterpillars and for yellowing.
